h: Avraham, the Ten Trials and the Cessation of Divine Wrath
Terach’s death marks Avraham’s repair of the primordial blemish through ten ascending trials, culminating in the Akeidah.
The End of Divine Wrath and Avraham's Repair

p: סִיּוּם הַפָּרָשָׁה וַיָּמָת תֶּרַח בְּחָרָן ופירש"י הַנּוּן הֲפוּכָה לוֹמַר לְךָ עַד אַבְרָם חֲוַן אַף שֶׁל מָקוֹם שֶׁכֵּיוָן שֶׁבָּא אַבְרָהָם לֹא הָיָה חֲרוֹן אַף וכמ"ש (ב"ר פ' ב) יִהְיֶה אוֹר זֶה אַבְרָהָם שֶׁהוּא בָּא לְתַקֵּן פְּגַם אדה"ר וכמ"ש (שָׁם פ' יד) הֲרֵי אֲנִי בּוֹרֵא אֶת הָאָדָם תְּחִלָּה שֶׁאִם יְקַלְקֵל יָבֹא אַבְרָהָם וִיתַקֵּן תַּחְתָּיו.

At the close of the parashah it says, 'Terach died in Haran.' Rashi explains that the letter nun is inverted, to teach that until Avram there was divine anger, whereas once Avraham arrived there was no longer anger. Bereishis Rabbah (chapter 2) identifies 'Let there be light' with Avraham: he came to repair the damage of Adam HaRishon. The Midrash (chapter 14) similarly says: 'I will first create Adam; if he corrupts [his state], Avraham will come and repair it in his stead.'

וּכְמוֹ שֶׁאָמַרְנוּ בַּעֲשָׂרָה דּוֹרוֹת שֶׁמִּנֹּחַ וְעַד אַבְרָהָם שֶׁאָמְרוּ עַד שֶׁבָּא אַבְרָהָם אָבִינוּ וְקִיבֵּל שְׂכַר כֻּולָּם שֶׁהָעֲשָׂרָה דּוֹרוֹת הָיוּ רְאוּיָם לְתַקֵּן כָּל פְּגַם הַנָּחָשׁ מִכֹּל וָכֹל שֶׁכֵּן מוֹרֶה מִסְפַּר עֲשָׂרָה כְּנֶגֶד עֶשֶׂר מִדּוֹת.

As explained regarding the ten generations from Noach to Avraham, of which the Mishnah says that Avraham arrived and received the reward of them all, those ten generations had been capable of completely repairing the serpent’s damage, as indicated by the number ten, corresponding to the ten divine attributes.

וְהֵם קִלְקְלוּ וּבָא אאע"ה שֶׁנִּתְנַסָּה בְּעֶשֶׂר נִסְיוֹנוֹת שֶׁהֵם ג"כ כְּנֶגֶד ע"ס וְקִיבֵּל שְׂכַר כֻּולָּם כָּל הַחַיּוּת והני"ק שֶׁהָיָה בְּהָעֶשְׂרֵה דּוֹרוֹת (ונת' מא' א) וְנִכְתַּב רֶמֶז זֶה שֶׁכְּשֶׁבָּא אַבְרָהָם לֹא הָיָה עוֹד חֲרוֹן אַף.

They failed, but Avraham Avinu came and underwent ten trials, likewise corresponding to the ten sefirot. He received the reward of them all—the vitality and holy sparks that had belonged to those generations, as explained in the first discourse. Thus Scripture hints that with Avraham’s arrival divine anger ceased.
בְּמִיתַת תֶּרַח שֶׁהָיָה אַחַר נִסָּיוֹן הַט' שֶׁהָיָה מַה שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר לוֹ גֵּרֵשׁ הָאָמַר הַזֹּאת וְאֶת בְּנָהּ.
That hint appears with Terach’s death, which followed Avraham’s ninth trial, the command, 'Drive out this slave woman and her son.'
דְּמִיתַת תֶּרַח הָיָה ב' שָׁנִים קֹודֶם עֲקֵידַת יִצְחָק וכמ"ש (ב"ר פ' נֹחַ) וַהֲלֹא קְבוּרָתוֹ שֶׁל תֶּרַח קָדְמָה לִקְבוּרָתָהּ שֶׁל שָׂרָה שְׁתֵּי שָׁנִים.
For Terach died two years before the Binding of Yitzchak, as Bereishis Rabbah (Parashas Chayei Sarah) states: 'Was not the burial of Terach two years before the burial of Sarah?'

paragraphs.text: Bereshit Rabbah 2:3: “Rabbi Yehuda bar Simon interpreted the verses regarding the generations. “The earth was emptiness and disorder” – this is Adam the first man, who became oblivion and nothingness. “And disorder” – this is Cain, who sought to restore the world to emptiness and disorder. “And darkness” – this is the generation of Enosh, based on the verse: “Their actions are in the dark and they say: Who sees us and who knows of us?” (Isaiah 29:15). “Upon the face of the depths” – this is the generation of the Flood, as it is stated: “On that day all the wellsprings of the great depths were breached” (Genesis 7:11). “And the spirit [ruaḥ] of God was hovering over the surface of the water” – based on the verse: “God passed a wind [ruaḥ] over the earth” (Genesis 8:1). The Holy One blessed be He said: ‘Until when will the world conduct itself in darkness? Let some light come.’ “God said: Let there be light” (Genesis 1:3) – this is Abraham. That is what is written [regarding Abraham]: “Who roused [he’ir] righteousness from the east?” (Isaiah 41:2). Do not read it as he’ir, but rather, he’ir. “God called the light, Day, and the darkness, He called Night. It was evening and it was morning, one day” (Genesis 1:5). “God called the light, Day” – this is Jacob. “And the darkness, He called Night” – this is Esau. “It was evening” – this is Esau; “and it was morning” – this is Jacob. “It was evening” – the evening of Esau; “and it was morning” – the morning of Jacob. “One day” – as it is stated: “There will be one day, it will be known to the Lord, that is not day and not night…” (Zechariah 14:7). Alternatively, “one day” – which the Holy One blessed be He provided him. Which is that? It is Yom Kippur.”

h: The Ten Trials and the Oral Torah

p: וְהַטַּעַם שֶׁנִּרְמַז כָּאן הוּא שֶׁבֵּירוּר אאע"ה בְּכָל הָעֶשֶׂר מִדּוֹת מִתַּתָּא לְעֵילָּא וְזֶה הַטַּעַם שֶׁנִּסָּיוֹן הָרִאשׁוֹן שֶׁהָיָה בְּאוֹר כַּשְׂדִּים לֹא נִזְכַּר בַּתּוֹרָה רַק בְּרֶמֶז.

The reason the allusion is placed here is that Avraham’s purification of the ten attributes proceeds from below upward. This also explains why the first trial, in the furnace of Ur Kasdim, is not explicitly recorded in the Torah but only alluded to.
וי"ל מִפְּנֵי שֶׁהוּא מְכֻוָּון נֶגֶד מִדַּת מַלְכוּת וְהוּא מִתּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה כמ"ש מַלְכוּת פֶּה תּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה.
We may suggest that it corresponds to the attribute of Malchus, which belongs to the Oral Torah, as the teaching says: 'Malchus is the mouth; we call it the Oral Torah.'

שעפ"י דִּין תּוֹרָה לֹא הָיָה נִצְרָךְ אאע"ה לִמְסֹור א"ע לְהַשְׁלִיכוֹ לַכִּבְשָׁן שב"נ אֵינוֹ מְצֻוֶּוה עַל קְדֻושָּׁה הַשֵּׁם כמ"ש (סַנְהֶדְרִין עַד:) וְשֶׁלֹּא לְאַבֵּד א"ע ב"נ מְצֻוֶּוה וּמֻוזְהָר וכמש"נ וְאַף אֶת דִּמְכֶם לְנַפְשֹׁתֵיכֶם וְגוֹ' וכמ"ש (ב"ר פ' לד) וּלְשָׁי' הָרַמְבַּ"ם (פ"ה מַה' יסוה"ת ה' ד) מִי שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר בּוֹ יַעֲבֹור וְאַל יֵהָרֵג וְנֶהֱרַג וְלֹא עָבַר הֲרֵי זֶה מִתְחַיֵּיב בְּנַפְשׁוֹ.

For according to Torah law, Avraham was not required to surrender himself to the furnace: a descendant of Noach is not commanded to sanctify God's Name at the cost of life, as stated in Sanhedrin 74b. Moreover, a descendant of Noach is warned against destroying his own life, as the verse says, 'But your blood, of your lives, I will demand' (Bereishis 9:5), as explained in Bereishis Rabbah chapter 34. According to the Rambam (Hilchos Yesodei HaTorah 5:4), one who is told to transgress rather than be killed, yet chooses to be killed, is accountable for his life.
וְרַק אאע"ה רָאָה לְצֹורֶךְ הַשָּׁעָה לְמִיגְדַּר מִלְּתָא לְקַדֵּשׁ ש"ש.
Rather, Avraham recognized an extraordinary need at that moment: to establish a protective safeguard and sanctify the Divine Name.
וּמָסַר עַצְמוֹ לְהַשְׁלִיכוֹ לַכִּבְשָׁן כְּדֵי שֶׁיִּתְפַּרְסֵם כְּבוֹד מַלְכוּתוֹ יִתֹּק.
He therefore surrendered himself to be cast into the furnace, so that the glory of God's kingship might become known.

וְזֶה מִשֹּׁורֶשׁ תּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה וכמ"ש תּוֹס' (יְבָמוֹת צ:) דִּבְלֹא נָבִיא ג"כ שָׁרִי לַעֲבֹור עַל ד"ת לְמִגְדַּר מִלְּתָא לְצֹורֶךְ הַשָּׁעָה רַק מִדְּאִתַּחְזַק אֵלִיָּהוּ בְּנֵיאוֹת סָמְכוּ עָלָיו בְּהַבְטָחָתוֹ בִּירִידַת אֵשׁ שֶׁיִּהְיֶה מִגְדַּר מִלְּתָא שֶׁיִּתְקַדֵּשׁ שְׁמוֹ שֶׁל הקב"ה ע"ש.

This action arose from the root of the Oral Torah. Tosafos (Yevamos 90b) explains that even without a prophet it can be permissible, for the needs of the hour, to suspend a Torah law as a protective safeguard. Because Eliyahu had been established as a prophet, people relied on his assurance that fire would descend, and that the resulting sanctification of God's Name would warrant the temporary measure.
וְכֵן רָאָה א"א ע"ה צֹורֶךְ הַשָּׁעָה לְקַדֵּשׁ ש"ש.
In the same way, Avraham Avinu discerned that the needs of the hour required sanctification of the Divine Name.

paragraphs.text: Sanhedrin 74b:8-10: “They asked Rabbi Ami: Is a Noahide commanded to sanctify the Name, or is he not commanded to sanctify the Name? Abaye said: Come and hear: Noahides were commanded seven commandments. If this were so, there would be eight! Rava said to him: The commandments and all their associated obligations. What was the conclusion? Rav Adda bar Ahavah said: They said in the academy, it is written: “May Hashem forgive your servant in this matter: when my master enters the house of Rimmon to bow there, leaning on my arm, and I bow.” And it is written: “He said to him, ‘Go in peace.’””

paragraphs.text: Bereshit Rabbah 34:13: ““Every crawling creature that lives shall be yours to eat; like green vegetation, I have given you everything” (Genesis 9:3). “But flesh with its life, its blood, you shall not eat” (Genesis 9:4). “Every crawling creature that lives…but flesh with its life, its blood [you shall not eat]” – Rabbi Yosei bar Aivu in the name of Rabbi Yoḥanan: Adam the first man, for whom the consumption of meat for pleasure was not permitted, was not warned regarding a limb taken from a living animal, but the descendants of Noah, for whom the consumption of meat for pleasure was permitted, were warned regarding a limb taken from a living animal. “But I will demand your blood of your lives; from every beast I will demand it, and from man; from every man for his brother, I will demand the life of man” (Genesis 9:5). “But [akh] [I will demand your blood of your lives]” – to include one who strangles himself. One might think that this applies [even] to cases like Saul? The verse states akh. One might think that this applies [even] to cases like Ḥananya, Mishael, and Azarya? The verse states akh. “From every beast” – this refers to one who makes his fellow man available to a wild beast to kill him. “From every man for his brother” – this refers to one who hires others to kill his fellow man. Another interpretation, “from every beast I will demand it” – these are the four kingdoms. “From man [adam], from every man for his brother” – this is Esau, as it is written: “Deliver me, please, from the hand of my brother, from the hand of Esau” (Genesis 32:12). “I will demand the life of man” – these are Israel, as it is stated: “You are My flock” (Ezekiel 34:17); “Flock of My pasture, you are man” (Ezekiel 34:31).”

paragraphs.text: Mishneh Torah, Foundations of the Torah 5:4: “If anyone about whom it is said: "Transgress and do not sacrifice your life," sacrifices his life and does not transgress, he is held accountable for his life. When anyone about whom it is said: "Sacrifice your life and do not transgress," sacrifices his life and does not transgress, he sanctifies [God's] name. If he does so in the presence of ten Jews, he sanctifies [God's] name in public, like Daniel, Chananiah, Mishael, Azariah, and Rabbi Akiva and his colleagues. These are those slain by [the wicked] kingdom, above whom there is no higher level. Concerning them, [Psalms 44:23] states: "For Your sake, we have been slain all day, we are viewed as sheep for the slaughter," and [Psalms 50:5] states: "Gather unto Me, My pious ones, those who have made a covenant with Me by slaughter." When anyone about whom it is said: "Sacrifice your life and do not transgress," transgresses instead of sacrificing his life, he desecrates [God's] name. If he does so in the presence of ten Jews, he desecrates [God's] name in public, nullifies [the fulfillment of] the positive commandment of the sanctification of [God's] name, and violates the negative commandment against the desecration of God's name. Nevertheless, since he was forced to transgress, he is not [punished by] lashing, and, needless to say, is not executed by the court even if he was forced to slay [a person]. The [punishments of] lashes and execution are administered only to one who transgresses voluntarily, [when the transgression is observed by] witnesses, and [when] a warning [was given], as [Leviticus 20:5] states concerning one who gives his children to [the worship of] Molech: "I will turn My face against that person." The oral tradition teaches [that we can infer]: "that person" and not one who is forced [to transgress, who transgresses] inadvertently, or [who transgresses] because of an error. If, concerning the worship of false gods, which is the most serious [of sins], a person who is forced to worship is not liable for karet, nor, needless to say, execution by a court, how much more so [does this principle apply] regarding the other mitzvot of the Torah? [Similarly,] regarding forbidden sexual relations, [Deuteronomy 22:26] states: "Do not do anything to the maiden." One who could, however, escape and flee from under the power of a wicked king and fails to do so is like a dog who returns [to lick] his vomit. He is considered as one who worships false gods willingly. He will be prevented from reaching the world to come and will descend to the lowest levels of Gehinnom.”

paragraphs.text: Tosafot on Yevamot 90b:6:1: “Regarding Eliyahu, why do we need the fact that he was established as a prophet? It appears that even without a prophet a court may transgress in order to safeguard the matter. Ri explains that because Eliyahu was established as a prophet, they relied upon his promise that fire would descend, and on that promise they slaughtered sacred offerings outside the Temple: through his merit and prayer, fire would descend from Heaven, safeguarding the matter by sanctifying the name of the Holy One, blessed be He, publicly, and thereby Israel would return to proper conduct.”

h: The Akeidah and the Final Purification

p: וע"כ לֹא נִזְכַּר נִסָּיוֹן זֶה בַּתּוֹרָה רַק בְּרֶמֶז וּכְמוֹ נִיסּוּךְ הַמַּיִם שֶׁהוּא הללמ"ס וְיֵשׁ מִמֶּנּוּ רַק רֶמֶז בַּתּוֹרָה וכמ"ש (תַּעֲנִית ב:) וְכֵן כָּל הַנִּסְיוֹנוֹת הֵם מְכֻוָּונִים נֶגֶד הַמִּדּוֹת מִתַּתָּא לְעֵילָּא עַד נִסָּיוֹן הַט' שֶׁהוּא נֶגֶד מִדַּת חָכְמָה שֶׁהוּא הִתְגַּלּוּת רִאשׁוֹן מִבְּרִיאַת יֵשׁ מֵאַיִן לְהַשָּׂגַת אָדָם וְהָוְיָא מִדָּה רִאשׁוֹנָה שֶׁיֵּשׁ בּוֹ קְצָת תְּפִיסָה.

Thus the Torah records that trial only by allusion, just as the water libation is a law given to Moshe at Sinai and merely hinted at in Scripture (Ta’anis 2b). All Avraham’s trials correspond to the attributes, progressing from below upward, until the ninth, corresponding to Chochmah—the first manifestation of creation from nothing that is at all accessible to human understanding.
וְאָז נִשְׁלַם אאע"ה בְּכָל מַה שֶּׁיּוּכַל לְהִתְבָּרֵר מִצִּדּוֹ.
At that point, Avraham had attained completion in everything that could be refined through his own efforts.
וְאַחַר כָּךְ נִסָּיוֹן הָעֲקֵידָה שֶׁמְּכַוֵּון נֶגֶד כ"ע שֶׁהוּא נֶעְלַם מִכָּל רַעְיוֹן.
Afterward came the trial of the Akeidah, corresponding to Kesser Elyon, which is hidden from all thought.
זֶה הַבֵּירוּר מִצַּד השי"ת שֶׁבֵּירֵר אוֹתוֹ בְּכָל עַד הַשֹּׁורֶשׁ וְזָכָה לִבְחִי' זָקֵן.
This refinement came from Hashem Himself, Who tested Avraham throughout, down to the root, until Avraham merited the designation 'elder.'
וע"כ אַחַר נִסָּיוֹן הַט' שֶׁהָיָה אָז מִיתַת תֶּרַח כְּמוֹ שֶׁזָּכַרְנוּ מהמ"ר.
Therefore, after the ninth trial—at the time of Terach’s death, as we have cited from the Midrash—
נִרְמַז בְּמֵתָתוֹ דְּכ' וַיָּמָת תֶּרַח בְּחָרָן שֶׁעַד אַבְרָם הָיָה חֲרוֹן אַף שֶׁל מָקוֹם.
his death hints through the words 'Terach died in Haran' that divine wrath had continued only until Avram.

שֶׁעַל יְדֵי אַבְרָהָם כָּלָה הֶחָרוֹן אַף שֶׁהוּא מִצִּדּוֹ כְּבָר תִּיקּוּן כָּל פְּגָם הַנָּחָשׁ בְּשֹׁורֶשׁ כְּפִי כֹּחוֹ כָּאָמוּר וְאַחַר כָּךְ הָיָה נִסָּיוֹן הָעֲקֵידָה שֶׁהָיָה הַבֵּירוּר מִצַּד השי"ת וְאַחַר כָּךְ כ' וְאַבְרָהָם זָקֵן בָּא בַּיָּמִים ובזהו"ק אֵי' ע"ז בְּיוֹמִין עִלָּאִין וְהַיְינוּ בַּג' רִאשׁוֹנוֹת שֶׁנִּשְׁלַם בְּכָל עָשָׂר הַמִּדּוֹת:

Through Avraham, that wrath ended, because he had already repaired the serpent’s primal blemish at its root to the fullest extent within human power. The Akeidah followed, a further refinement from the Divine side; and afterward Scripture says, 'Avraham was old, advanced in days.' The Zohar interprets 'in days' as referring to the supernal days—the first three attributes—in which he reached completion.

paragraphs.text: Maharal, Derech Chaim on Avos 5:3, paragraph 13: “Furthermore, just as the world was created through ten utterances, because the world contains a higher, transcendent level indicated by the number ten, so Avraham was tested specifically through ten trials. Through these ten trials, Avraham likewise became entirely separate from nature, for this is the meaning of trial, as explained. The same applies to every number ten mentioned: all come to explain this matter, as will be explained further.”

reviewedSourceExcerpt.he: ועוד, כמו שנברא העולם בעשרה מאמרות, מפני שיש בעולם מדריגה עליונה נבדלת אשר מורה על זה מספר עשרה, כך נתנסה אברהם בי' נסיונות דוקא, כי על ידי אלו עשרה נסיונות נעשה אברהם גם כן נבדל מן הטבע לגמרי. שזהו ענין הנסיון, כמו שהתבאר. וכן כל מספר י' שזכר, שכולם באו לפרש דבר זה, וכמו שיתבאר עוד.
reviewedSourceExcerpt.en: Furthermore, just as the world was created through ten utterances, because the world contains a higher, transcendent level indicated by the number ten, so Avraham was tested specifically through ten trials. Through these ten trials, Avraham likewise became entirely separate from nature, for this is the meaning of trial, as explained. The same applies to every number ten mentioned: all come to explain this matter, as will be explained further.
